newsitem.title: USA: Insituform Tech cost cuts to aid 2nd half.
newsitem.headline: Insituform Tech cost cuts to aid 2nd half.

text.p: Insituform Technologies Inc said financial effects of its current cost-cutting efforts could begin to be felt in the second half of this year.
Anthony Hooper, president and chief executive officer, said the company was making good progress in those efforts as well as in reversing a trend of declining margins.

He made the statement as the company reported net income in the first quarter of 1997 dropped to $1.081 million or $.04 per share, compared to $2.25 million or $.08 per share in the same period last year, on revenues of $77.082 million, up 13.2 percent from $68.11 million, a year ago.

The company said reduction in gross margins in its core business was the principal cause of the earnings decline, which it said was mainly due to internal problems of high cost and inefficient use of resources.
Hooper said the company has reduced field headcount by 12 percent as of April 30 and has identified at least another 4.0 percent to cut during the balance of the year, he said.
Hooper said the company was proceeding with plans to consolidate two head offices into single location in St. Louis and reorganize its core North American rehabilitation business.
"We intend to continue our focus on the core sewer rehabilitation business and its cost structure," he added.
